relations.counterexample_control: Unbounded monotone sequence x_n = n has no supremum in R and diverges.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: Every bounded above subset of R has a least upper bound.
relations.quantifier_signature: LUB_PROPERTY(R) => FORALL(x_seq monotone increasing, bounded above) [x_seq -> sup(range(x_seq))]
relations.relational_transformation: Set E = {x_n : n in N}. E is non-empty and bounded above, so L = sup E exists. By sup definition, for all eps > 0 exists N such that x_N > L - eps. Since x_n is increasing, for all n >= N, L - eps < x_N <= x_n <= L < L + eps, proving x_n -> L.
relations.witness_invariant: L = sup{x_n} AND FORALL(eps > 0) EXISTS(N in N) FORALL(n >= N) [|x_n - L| < eps]

relations.counterexample_control: In Q (incomplete), sequence approximating sqrt(2) is Cauchy but has no limit in Q.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: R is an Archimedean ordered field with LUB property.
relations.quantifier_signature: FORALL(seq (x_n) in R) [is_cauchy(x_n) <=> is_convergent(x_n)]
relations.relational_transformation: Convergent => Cauchy by triangle inequality |x_n - x_m| <= |x_n - L| + |x_m - L| < eps. Cauchy => Bounded => Has convergent subseq x_{n_k} -> L by Bolzano-Weierstrass => Full sequence x_n -> L by Cauchy property.

relations.counterexample_control: Nested open intervals (0, 1/n) have empty intersection.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: I_n = [a_n, b_n] is nested sequence of closed bounded intervals.
relations.quantifier_signature: LUB_PROPERTY(R) => EXISTS(x in R) FORALL(n in N) [x in I_n]
relations.relational_transformation: The set of left endpoints A = {a_n : n in N} is bounded above by any right endpoint b_k. Thus x = sup A exists. For all n, a_n <= x <= b_n, so x in bigcap I_n.
relations.witness_invariant: sup{a_n} <= inf{b_n} AND bigcap I_n != empty

relations.counterexample_control: Unbounded sequence x_n = (-1)^n * n has no convergent subsequence.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: Sequence (x_n) is bounded in R.
relations.quantifier_signature: is_bounded(x_seq) => EXISTS(n_k, L) [x_{n_k} -> L]
relations.relational_transformation: Repeated bisection of bounding interval [a, b] produces nested intervals I_k containing infinitely many sequence terms. By nested interval theorem, bigcap I_k = {L}, and term selection yields convergent subsequence x_{n_k} -> L.

relations.counterexample_control: Divergent series sum 1/n does not satisfy Cauchy criterion.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: sum_{k=1}^infty |a_k| < infty.
relations.quantifier_signature: converges(sum |a_k|) => converges(sum a_k)
relations.relational_transformation: By Cauchy criterion for series, |sum_{k=m}^n a_k| <= sum_{k=m}^n |a_k| < eps. Since partial sums of absolute values are Cauchy, partial sums of original series are Cauchy in R, hence converge.

relations.counterexample_control: Dirichlet function or Heaviside jump fails sequential continuity along x_n = 1/n vs -1/n.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: f: A -> R, x0 in A.
relations.quantifier_signature: is_eps_delta_continuous(f, x0) <=> (FORALL(x_n -> x0) [f(x_n) -> f(x0)])
relations.relational_transformation: (=>) If |x - x0| < delta => |f(x) - f(x0)| < eps, choosing N for delta gives |f(x_n) - f(x0)| < eps. (<=) If eps-delta fails for eps0, construct x_n in B(x0, 1/n) with |f(x_n) - f(x0)| >= eps0, contradicting sequential continuity.

relations.counterexample_control: Open interval (0, 1) is bounded but not closed; cover {(1/n, 1)} has no finite subcover.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: K subset R.
relations.quantifier_signature: is_compact(K) <=> (is_closed(K) AND is_bounded(K))
relations.relational_transformation: In R^n, every open cover of a closed bounded set admits a finite subcover via binary bisection and Bolzano-Weierstrass.

relations.counterexample_control: f(x) = x on open interval (0, 1) has sup = 1 not achieved in (0, 1).
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: K subset R is compact, f: K -> R is continuous.
relations.quantifier_signature: is_compact(K) AND is_continuous(f, K) => EXISTS(x_min, x_max in K) [f(x_min) <= f(x) <= f(x_max)]
relations.relational_transformation: Continuous image of compact set f(K) is compact in R (closed and bounded). Therefore M = sup f(K) and m = inf f(K) belong to f(K), so there exist x_max, x_min in K with f(x_max) = M, f(x_min) = m.
relations.witness_invariant: sup(f(K)) in f(K) AND inf(f(K)) in f(K)

relations.counterexample_control: f(x) = 1/x on non-compact (0, 1) is continuous but not uniformly continuous.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: K subset R is compact, f: K -> R is continuous.
relations.quantifier_signature: is_compact(K) AND is_continuous(f, K) => is_uniformly_continuous(f, K)
relations.relational_transformation: For eps > 0, for each x in K exists delta_x > 0 with |f(y) - f(x)| < eps/2 on B(x, delta_x). The collection {B(x, delta_x / 2)} covers K. By compactness, finite subcover exists. Setting delta = min(delta_i / 2) > 0 gives uniform modulus.

relations.counterexample_control: f(x) = sqrt(x) on [0, 1] is uniformly continuous by Heine-Cantor, but non-Lipschitz since derivative is unbounded as x -> 0+.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: f: A -> R is Lipschitz continuous with constant M > 0: |f(x) - f(y)| <= M |x - y|.
relations.quantifier_signature: is_lipschitz(f, M) => FORALL(eps > 0) EXISTS(delta = eps / M) FORALL(x, y) [|x - y| < delta => |f(x) - f(y)| < eps]
relations.relational_transformation: Given Lipschitz bound |f(x) - f(y)| <= M |x - y|, for any eps > 0 set delta = eps / M. Then |x - y| < delta implies |f(x) - f(y)| <= M (eps / M) = eps, proving uniform continuity.

relations.counterexample_control: Discontinuous sign function sgn(x) maps [-1, 1] to {-1, 0, 1} (disconnected), failing intermediate value property.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: Interval [a, b] is connected in R, f is continuous on [a, b].
relations.quantifier_signature: is_connected([a, b]) AND f in C([a, b]) => is_connected(f([a, b])) => y in [f(a), f(b)] => EXISTS(c) [f(c) = y]
relations.relational_transformation: Continuous image of a connected set is connected. Connected subsets of R are intervals. Thus f([a, b]) contains the interval between f(a) and f(b), so every intermediate value y is achieved at some c in [a, b].
relations.witness_invariant: c = sup{x in [a, b] : f(x) < y} AND f(c) = y

relations.counterexample_control: Heaviside step function is not continuous at 0, hence not differentiable.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: f is differentiable at x0.
relations.quantifier_signature: is_differentiable(f, x0) => is_continuous(f, x0)
relations.relational_transformation: f(x) - f(x0) = ((f(x) - f(x0))/(x - x0)) * (x - x0). Taking limits as x -> x0: lim (f(x) - f(x0)) = f'(x0) * 0 = 0, proving lim_{x->x0} f(x) = f(x0).

relations.counterexample_control: f(x) = |x| on [-1, 1] satisfies f(-1)=f(1) but lacks differentiability at interior extremum x=0.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: f continuous on [a, b], differentiable on (a, b), f(a) = f(b).
relations.quantifier_signature: EVT(f, [a, b]) AND FERMAT_STATIONARY(f, (a, b)) => EXISTS(c in (a, b)) [f'(c) = 0]
relations.relational_transformation: By EVT, f attains maximum M and minimum m on [a, b]. If M = m, f is constant and f'(c) = 0 everywhere. Otherwise at least one extremum c is in open (a, b). By Fermat's stationary point theorem, f'(c) = 0.
relations.witness_invariant: c in argmax(f) cap (a, b) OR c in argmin(f) cap (a, b) => f'(c) = 0

relations.counterexample_control: f(x) = |x| on [-1, 1] has secant slope 0 but no point with derivative 0.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: f continuous on [a, b], differentiable on (a, b).
relations.quantifier_signature: ROLLES_THEOREM => FORALL(f in C([a, b]) cap D((a, b))) EXISTS(c in (a, b)) [f(b) - f(a) = f'(c)(b - a)]
relations.relational_transformation: Define auxiliary function g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - ((f(b)-f(a))/(b-a))*(x - a). g is continuous on [a, b], differentiable on (a, b), and g(a) = g(b) = 0. By Rolle's theorem on g, exists c in (a, b) with g'(c) = 0 => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a).

relations.counterexample_control: If g is discontinuous at endpoint, Cauchy MVT relation fails.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: f, g continuous on [a, b], differentiable on (a, b).
relations.quantifier_signature: ROLLES_THEOREM => EXISTS(c in (a, b)) [(f(b) - f(a))g'(c) = (g(b) - g(a))f'(c)]
relations.relational_transformation: Define auxiliary function h(x) = [g(b) - g(a)]f(x) - [f(b) - f(a)]g(x). h is continuous on [a, b], differentiable on (a, b), and h(a) = h(b) = g(b)f(a) - f(b)g(a). By Rolle's theorem, exists c in (a, b) with h'(c) = 0 => (f(b) - f(a))g'(c) = (g(b) - g(a))f'(c).

relations.counterexample_control: Non-smooth function f(x) = |x|^3 has undefined 4th derivative.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: f in C^n([a, b]), f^{(n+1)} exists on (a, b).
relations.quantifier_signature: TAYLOR_CONSTRUCTION => |f(x) - P_n(x)| <= (M_{n+1}/(n+1)!) |x - x0|^{n+1}
relations.relational_transformation: Construct Taylor polynomial P_n(x) matching derivatives at x0 up to order n. Applying Generalized Rolle's Theorem to remainder function yields exact Lagrange remainder term (f^{(n+1)}(xi)/(n+1)!)(x - x0)^{n+1}.

relations.counterexample_control: Dirichlet indicator function 1_Q is discontinuous everywhere and non-integrable (U - L = 1).
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: f is uniformly continuous on compact interval [a, b].
relations.quantifier_signature: is_uniformly_continuous(f, [a, b]) => is_riemann_integrable(f, [a, b])
relations.relational_transformation: For eps > 0, choose delta > 0 such that |x - y| < delta => |f(x) - f(y)| < eps/(b-a). Choose partition P with mesh width < delta. Then M_i - m_i < eps/(b-a), so U(f, P) - L(f, P) = sum (M_i - m_i) Delta x_i < eps.
relations.witness_invariant: mesh(P) < delta => U(f, P) - L(f, P) < eps

relations.counterexample_control: Discontinuous integrand produces non-differentiable integral accumulator.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: f is continuous on [a, b], F(x) = int_a^x f(t)dt.
relations.quantifier_signature: f in C([a, b]) => FORALL(x in (a, b)) [F'(x) = f(x)]
relations.relational_transformation: (F(x+h) - F(x))/h = (1/h) int_x^{x+h} f(t)dt. By Mean Value Theorem for integrals, exists c_h between x and x+h with (1/h) int_x^{x+h} f(t)dt = f(c_h). As h -> 0, c_h -> x, and by continuity f(c_h) -> f(x).

relations.counterexample_control: Pointwise limit of f_n(x) = x^n on [0, 1] is discontinuous at x=1 (0 for x < 1, 1 at x = 1).
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: f_n continuous on A, f_n -> f uniformly on A.
relations.quantifier_signature: (FORALL(n) f_n in C(A)) AND f_n -> f uniformly => f in C(A)
relations.relational_transformation: Standard eps/3 argument: |f(x) - f(x0)| <= |f(x) - f_N(x)| + |f_N(x) - f_N(x0)| + |f_N(x0) - f(x0)| < eps/3 + eps/3 + eps/3 = eps.

relations.counterexample_control: Pointwise spike sequence f_n(x) = 2n x e^{-n x^2} on [0, 1] has pointwise limit 0 but int_0^1 f_n = 1 - e^{-n} -> 1 != 0.
relations.mathematical_hypotheses: f_n Riemann integrable on [a, b], f_n -> f uniformly on [a, b].
relations.quantifier_signature: (FORALL(n) f_n in R([a, b])) AND f_n -> f uniformly => lim int_a^b f_n = int_a^b (lim f_n)
relations.relational_transformation: |int_a^b f_n(x)dx - int_a^b f(x)dx| <= int_a^b |f_n(x) - f(x)|dx <= sup_{x in [a, b]} |f_n(x) - f(x)| * (b - a) < (eps / (b - a)) * (b - a) = eps.
